name: Raven Industries on How Autonomy Is Changing Agriculture
title: Raven Industries on How Autonomy Is Changing Agriculture
answer: This is a news article published by Raven Industries, a precision agriculture technology company, in April 2022. It argues that automating farm equipment demands more advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning than automating transportation, because driverless agricultural machines must control chemical application levels and boom height as well as perceive and avoid obstacles. It describes Raven's commercialized driverless solutions and the efficiency, sustainability and labour benefits the company attributes to autonomy.

sections.body: The source is a news article on the website of Raven Industries, published on April 26, 2022, under the title 10 Ways Autonomy Is Changing Agriculture. Raven describes itself in the article as a leader in precision agriculture technology for over 40 years. The piece is a company news item rather than an independent study, and it sets out the company's view of how autonomous technology is affecting farming, drawing on its own products and investments.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The article's central argument is that automating agricultural equipment can require more advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities than automating transportation, because driverless agricultural technology must also precisely control chemical application levels and boom height alongside safety and object perception and avoidance. Raven states it had two commercialized driverless solutions on the market and was investing in autonomous technology for agriculture because it solves real challenges in farming today. The claimed benefits are efficiency, with more field coverage using less labour, more precise herbicide application with less chemical use, and more fuel-efficient driving with less crop damage. Adoption is said to free hundreds of labour hours for farmers to reallocate. Sustainability benefits are described as preventing chemical drift and reducing fuel emissions through automatic drive path planning. At harvest, Raven OMNiDRIVE, described as an automatically syncing driverless tractor, lets one driver complete a full harvest with virtually no spills. Autonomy also lets farmers manage fields and fleets remotely through Raven Slingshot Connected Workflow and make real-time data-driven decisions. Automating individual functions, such as VSN Visual Guidance's camera navigation of crop rows, is said to reduce operator fatigue and accident risk, while AutoBoom XRT automatically adjusts sprayer boom height to prevent damage. The article adds that automation makes operations easier to scale, and that widespread adoption of autonomous vehicles in agriculture will make it easier to manage hundreds of fields from a centralized system. Raven says the fully autonomous farming future will raise yields and lower operating costs, and it recruits engineers to drive agriculture forward with artificial intelligence and machine learning.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The article states that Raven had two commercialized driverless solutions on the market and had been a precision agriculture technology leader for over 40 years. It claims autonomous adoption frees hundreds of labour hours for farmers to reallocate. It names Raven OMNiDRIVE, Raven Slingshot Connected Workflow, VSN Visual Guidance and AutoBoom XRT as products. No other figures are given.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in agriculture gets a supplier's account of where machine learning sits in farm autonomy. The most useful point is the claim that agricultural autonomy is harder than transport autonomy because the same system must control chemical application levels and boom height as well as perceive and avoid obstacles. The article also maps AI and automation onto named products, from camera-based row navigation to automatic boom height adjustment and fleet workflow, which shows how the equipment layer beyond Deere is being positioned.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Agriculture

sections.body: The article is company news published by Raven Industries in April 2022, so it presents the vendor's own view and promotes its products and recruitment. It gives no independent data, trial results or cost figures, and the claims about labour hours, yields and operating costs are stated without evidence. It does not cover competing systems or the regulatory side of autonomous equipment.
